senses.gloss: To want a particular price for something you are selling.
examples: How much are they *asking* for the house on the corner?
He *asked* too much for the old truck, so nobody bought it.
Don't *ask* more than the car is actually worth.

senses.gloss: To invite someone to an event or to your home.
examples: They *asked* nearly a hundred people to the wedding.
We're *asking* the neighbors to dinner on Saturday.
I haven't *asked* him to the party yet.

senses.gloss: To take on a duty, a position of power, or a responsibility.
senses.ru: принимать на себя, взять на себя (обязанности); вступать в должность
examples: She *assumed* command of the unit in March.
The buyer will *assume* the rest of the debt.
He has *assumed* full responsibility for the mistake.

senses.gloss: To put on a manner, an appearance, or a name that is not really your own.
senses.ru: принимать (вид), напускать на себя; присваивать (чужое имя)
examples: He *assumed* an air of total innocence.
The spy had *assumed* a new identity before crossing the border.
Actors often *assume* an accent for a role.

senses.gloss: To consider something to have a particular amount of importance or value.
examples: I don't *attach* much importance to rumors.
The court *attached* great weight to the witness's testimony.
Younger voters are *attaching* more significance to the issue than their parents did.

senses.gloss: To criticize someone or something strongly and publicly.
examples: Don't *attack* the person; argue with the idea.
The senator *attacked* the plan as a handout to big banks.
Newspapers have been *attacking* the mayor for weeks.

senses.gloss: To begin work on something with great energy.
senses.ru: энергично браться за, приниматься за, взяться
examples: Let's *attack* the hardest problem first.
She *attacked* the pile of dishes as soon as the guests left.
They're *attacking* the backlog one order at a time.

senses.gloss: Of a disease, chemical, or insect, to damage something by acting on it.
examples: The virus *attacks* the nervous system.
The disease *attacked* his joints first.
Termites had been *attacking* the beams for years before anyone looked.

senses.gloss: To attend a college course without taking the exams or earning credit.
senses.ru: слушать курс вольнослушателем, посещать без зачёта
examples: You can *audit* the course for free if you don't need the credit.
She *audited* two graduate seminars before she applied.
I'm *auditing* a Spanish class this semester.

senses.gloss: To turn your eyes or face away from something you do not want to see.
examples: She *averted* her eyes when the nurse pulled the needle out.
Most people *avert* their gaze and keep walking.
He sat through the whole scene with his face *averted*.

senses.gloss: To make a vehicle move backward.
examples: *Back* the truck a little closer to the ramp.
She *backed* the car slowly down the narrow driveway.
He was *backing* the van when he hit the mailbox.

senses.gloss: To catch or kill an animal while hunting, or informally, to succeed in getting something.
examples: They hope to *bag* two turkeys this fall.
He *bagged* a twelve-point buck on the last day of the season.
She's *bagged* the biggest account in the office.

senses.gloss: To block a way physically, or to fasten a door with a bar.
examples: A fallen tree *barred* the road for two days.
He *barred* the door and put out the lamp.
Two guards stood in the doorway, *barring* the entrance.

senses.gloss: To say something in a loud, sharp voice, especially an order.
examples: Don't *bark* at me; I'm doing my best.
The sergeant *barked* an order and everyone stood up.
She was *barking* instructions from the kitchen all evening.

senses.gloss: To sew cloth together with long loose stitches that will be taken out later.
examples: *Baste* the seam before you sew it on the machine.
She *basted* the hem so it wouldn't shift.
The lining had been *basted* in place with white thread.

senses.gloss: To open and close your eyelashes quickly, often to charm someone.
examples: Don't *bat* your lashes at me — I know you broke it.
She *batted* her eyelashes at him and he turned red.
He signed the check without *batting* an eye.

senses.gloss: To cover something completely in light or color.
examples: Streetlights *bathe* the parking lot in a cold blue glow.
The sunset *bathed* the whole valley in orange.
The room was *bathed* in candlelight.

senses.gloss: To seem very attractive or inviting to someone.
examples: After a long winter, the beach *beckons*.
A career in medicine *beckoned*, but she chose music instead.
The open road was *beckoning*, so we packed the car and left.

senses.gloss: To lift a weight while lying on your back on a bench.
examples: He can *bench* two hundred and twenty-five pounds.
She *benched* more than anyone else on the team.
I've been *benching* three times a week since January.

senses.gloss: To crowd around someone, or to overwhelm them with requests and questions.
examples: Reporters *besieged* the family's front porch.
The office is *besieged* with calls every time prices change.
Fans have been *besieging* the station with requests all week.

senses.gloss: To show a feeling you were trying to hide, without meaning to.
examples: His face *betrays* nothing.
Her voice *betrayed* how nervous she was.
A slight tremor in his hands had *betrayed* him.

senses.gloss: To advertise or describe something publicly as being a particular thing.
examples: The company *bills* itself as the cheapest carrier in the state.
The fight was *billed* as the match of the century.
They're *billing* the new place as a family restaurant.

senses.gloss: To turn pale suddenly from fear or shock.
examples: She *blanches* at the sight of a needle.
He *blanched* when he saw the hospital bill.
I could see him *blanching* as the numbers went up.

senses.gloss: To criticize someone or something very harshly in public.
examples: The governor *blasted* the plan as reckless.
Critics have *blasted* the film for its ending.
Union leaders are *blasting* the company over the layoffs.

senses.gloss: To play music or a radio at a very high volume.
senses.ru: врубать на всю громкость; греметь (о музыке)
examples: The neighbors *blast* their music every Saturday night.
He *blasted* the radio all the way to Denver.
Country music was *blasting* from the open windows.

senses.gloss: To make someone unable to notice or judge something clearly.
senses.ru: ослеплять, ослепить (перен.); лишать способности видеть правду
examples: Don't let loyalty *blind* you to what he did.
Greed *blinded* him to the risks.
She has been *blinded* by her own success.

senses.gloss: To live somewhere paying for meals and a room, or to keep an animal for pay.
senses.ru: жить на пансионе, снимать с питанием; держать (животное) за плату
examples: She *boards* with a family near campus.
We *boarded* the dog for a week while we were away.
He was *boarding* at a house on Elm Street that winter.

senses.gloss: To run away suddenly and fast, usually out of fear.
examples: Don't *bolt* for the door the second the bell rings.
The horse *bolted* at the sound of the gun.
The deer had *bolted* before I could raise the camera.

senses.gloss: To swallow food very quickly, almost without chewing.
examples: Don't *bolt* your food; you'll get a stomachache.
He *bolted* his breakfast and ran for the bus.
She was *bolting* a sandwich between meetings.

senses.gloss: To fail badly, especially a movie, a performance, or a test (informal).
examples: He *bombed* the chemistry final and had to retake the class.
Nobody wants to *bomb* in front of a live audience.
The movie had *bombed* in theaters before streaming saved it.

senses.gloss: To direct a great many questions, messages, or demands at someone.
examples: Reporters *bombarded* her with questions about the deal.
We are *bombarded* with ads from the moment we wake up.
Stop *bombarding* me with texts; I'll answer tonight.

senses.gloss: To join two surfaces firmly, or to stick fast to a material.
examples: This glue *bonds* metal to plastic in about a minute.
The layers are *bonded* with heat, not stitching.
The resin hadn't *bonded* properly, so the handle came off.

senses.gloss: To record someone's name and the charge against them at a police station.
examples: They *booked* him on suspicion of theft.
He was *booked* and released within an hour.
The officer spent the whole evening *booking* three suspects.
